newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan journalist gets six months prison term.
newsitem.headline: Jordan journalist gets six months prison term.

text.p: A civil court has sentenced a Jordanian journalist to six months in prison for publishing an interview it said spread an outlawed Islamist party doctrine, lawyers said on Sunday.

Abdullah Bin Issa, 27, was found guilty last Thursday by Amman's civil court of "publishing statements that propagated views" of the illegal Hizb al-Tahrir party (Islamic Liberation Party), and of publishing material that slandered King Hussein and the royal family, his lawyers added.
Bin Issa said he planned to appeal the ruling this week.

"I am confident of the justice of my case and that the appeal I plan to make against the sentence will achieve my innocence, God willing," Bin Issa, who is currently the editor of the Amman-based weekly Al-Hayat told Reuters.
Bin Issa was taken to court last year for publishing an interview in October 1995 with the head of the outlawed Hizb al-Tahrir party Ata Abu al-Rishtah in the weekly al-Hiwar magazine.
Lawyers said Abu al-Rishtah, who has a long prison record, did not mention King Hussein in person but strongly attacked the government for making peace with Israel, calling it "atheistic".
Abu al-Rishtah's party also advocate an Islamic Caliphate rule in the Arab world.
